about: Every source consulted for the Service-page and Mileage research, with its licence, what was actually read, and what was done with it. 'accessed' is the day this research read it. A source read only through a search summary says so: the search summary is not the document.

evidenceLevels.E1: A lead: the function is known to exist (closed tool, vendor claim, forum post) but no protocol detail is public.
evidenceLevels.E2: A public definition (standard, community data) that says where a value is. Not reviewed against a vehicle by this project.
evidenceLevels.E3: The vehicle maker's own document names the procedure or tool function for an exact vehicle (owner's manual, service bulletin). For a dashboard-level reset that is the whole procedure; for a scan-tool function it names the module and the function but does not publish the request.
evidenceLevels.E4: Reviewed against a recorded exchange of that exact vehicle (read-only observation).
evidenceLevels.E5: Verified on that exact vehicle by this project: write or routine, read-back and dashboard result, with hashed evidence (the project's own promotion checklist). No operation in the repository has this.

licenceRules: Data under CC BY-SA 4.0 (OBDb, Wikipedia text) may be used with attribution; anything derived from it is offered under the same licence. The tables in this folder that count OBDb definitions are such derivatives: see README.md.
MIT data (opendbc) may be used with the licence notice.
GPL-3.0 and ODbL data are not merged into the app. They stay leads (the project already quarantines both in the shipped catalog).
A repository with no licence is all rights reserved: a lead only, nothing is copied.
Commercial tools, closed software and vendor documents prove that a function exists. Nothing is copied from them and no behaviour is inferred from them.

sources.name: OBDb vehicle signal sets (GitHub organisation OBDb, one repository per vehicle)
sources.licenceChecked: 2026-10-19 through the GitHub API: all 880 vehicle repositories report CC-BY-SA-4.0. The organisation README says the text is mostly CC BY-SA 4.0. Infrastructure repositories differ (vscode-obdb is Apache-2.0; the website and editor repositories have none) and were not used.
sources.accessed: 2026-10-18 (default signal sets); 2026-10-19 (all 860 downloaded vehicle repositories, including tests and year-range files; the shipped catalog)
sources.read: The default signal set of every vehicle repository, and the OBDb rows of the catalog the app ships (source id 5, revision 3fd5afe5ecf68a6d6b06beb7b4e86f23ee6df69b of 2026-10-17; the catalog's meta table records a different revision, bc13d91a..., 2026-10-03).
sources.use: Counted, never copied: the coverage tables in this folder are derived from it. The app already bundles it with attribution (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
limits: All commands are read services (22, 21, 01); there is no write, routine or security-access command.
About 60% of the rows in the shipped catalog are flagged debug, and 61,598 more carry a dbgfilter (debug in some model years) that the catalog dropped.
The catalog has no model-year filter; OBDb has one per command (filter) and, in four repositories, year-range signal sets.
A definition is community work. Its being listed does not mean a car answers it; a recorded reply (obdb-tests) is the evidence that one did.

sources.name: OBDb signal set JSON schema (OBDb/.schemas, signals.json)
sources.read: The schema file (the 'dbg' flag: 'Whether to debug the signal responses'; filterObject: from, to, years) and the Python reference code: can/signals.py (Filter.matches, the year semantics), signalsets/loader.py and year_range.py (which signal set applies to a year), signals_testing.py (the layout of the tests).
sources.use: Wording of the 'definition is still marked as under test' line; the exact year semantics implemented in Services/OemDiagnostics/ObdbYearEvidence.cs and research/tools/evidence-obdb.js.
limits: The schema does not say 'unverified'. The app words the flag as 'still marked as under test in the catalog' and no stronger.

sources.name: commaai/opendbc (CAN message definitions)
sources.accessed: 2026-10-17 (upstream clone, commit 48c7f06c6f27c41e7169242acb03ef9775658deb); 2026-10-19 (the copy inside the shipped catalog)
sources.read: The odometer-named signals of the DBC files (upstream and as imported), and for this round the Ford oil messages in ford_lincoln_base_pt.dbc and ford_cgea1_2_ptcan_2011.dbc: Cluster_Info1_FD1 0x430 (EngOilLife_B_RqReset, bit 43), EngineData_7 0x179 / Engine_Data_7_CG1 0x159 (EngOilLife_Pc_Actl, 7 bits), EngineData_17 0x17D (EngOilLife_T_Actl, DistToNextOilChange, EngOilSrvcMsgTxt_D_Rq); a search of every DBC for oil, service and maintenance found no GM or BMW oil-life or reset signal.
sources.use: Already used by the app (BroadcastOdometerProvider). The Ford messages are recorded as the mechanism of the dashboard reset and as a way to recognise a reset in a recording; nothing is sent or decoded by the app.
limits: The catalog records no revision for its opendbc snapshot ('user-provided snapshot').
Several odometer signals give no unit or scale.

sources.name: Wikipedia, OBD-II PIDs
sources.read: Rows for PIDs 21, 31, 4D, 4E, 5B, 5C and A6 (4E: name only), and the whole page for any PID about oil life, service or maintenance: only 5C, engine oil temperature, mentions oil.
sources.use: Confirms the standard odometer PID (A6: four bytes, divided by 10, km) and that no standard PID exists for oil life or a service interval. Facts only; no text is copied.
limits: A public summary of SAE J1979; the standard (paid) was not read.

sources.name: ludwig-v/arduino-psa-diag
sources.read: Cloned and searched for oil, service, maintenance and reset: the repository documents UDS session and unlock services for PSA coding zones (BMF, TELEMAT) and DTC tables; it has no service reset.
sources.use: Not used. The project already quarantines its data in the shipped catalog (source id 4, 0 active rows).
limits: GPL-3.0 cannot be merged into the closed app.

sources.name: FORScan change history
sources.read: The whole page (284,883 characters) in three parts. The tool reported the 2.3.40 section of the first part as cut off.
sources.use: Proof that per-vehicle PCM service procedures 'Reset oil change indicator' and 'Reset Engine Oil Deterioration Learned Value' exist for named Ford and Mazda models (2.1.14 to 2.3.67). Names the vehicles only.
limits: No request bytes are public.
Since 2.3.46 FORScan shows manual instructions when a PCM does not support the function.

sources.name: Ross-Tech Wiki, SRI Reset Procedure
sources.accessed: 2026-10-19 (the SRI Reset page, the VW Golf VII cluster page and the Audi service-interval page, each in full)
sources.read: In the instrument cluster (module 17, adaptation) the items 'ESI: Resetting ESI', 'FIX: Distance covered since last mileage-dependent inspection', 'FIX: Time since last time-dependent inspection', 'SID / SIA: maximum value of distance / time to service'; numbered channels 02 and 05 to 08 for older Audis. No identifier or request bytes on any of the pages.
sources.use: Shapes the operation taxonomy (reset versus set interval; oil versus inspection). No request bytes are given and none is used.
limits: Procedure level only.

sources.name: GM service bulletins hosted by NHTSA (for example MC-10114191-9999, MC-10246678-9999)
sources.accessed: 2026-10-19 (search summary only; the PDFs were not opened)
sources.read: The search summary says that a 2013 bulletin tells the technician to use a scan tool to reset the Engine Oil Life Remaining back to the percentage recorded before an ECM reprogramming, and that a later bulletin describes how the monitor works. [Superseded on 2026-10-19: the bulletin was downloaded and read in full, see gm-bulletin-12312a.]
sources.use: Superseded by gm-bulletin-12312a.
limits: Second-hand: confirm in the PDF before relying on the wording.

sources.name: GM Tech forum, 'Oil life monitor class 2 data'
sources.read: A post shows one Mode 22 request for oil life on a Bosch ECM; the poster saw the value fall to zero at shutdown and found the reset value in a broadcast, not in a Mode 22 reply.
sources.use: Not used.
limits: Unverified, single module, no reset.

sources.name: l77rodeo/gmlan (cited by the project's own candidate family.gm.engine-oil-life-reset)
sources.licence: none (the GitHub API reports no licence)
sources.accessed: 2026-10-19 (README read in full; the capture file was not opened)
sources.read: README: high-speed GMLAN messages from an E38 PCM and T43 TCM car. 0x1F1 (sent by the gateway) lists 'Engine oil life reset request' together with the power-takeoff and remote-start requests and the immobilizer pre-release password; 0x1F3 lists 'Transmission oil life reset request'. No bit layout is given.
sources.use: Recorded as the mechanism of the GM dashboard reset; the app never sends 0x1F1 because the same frame carries a remote-start request and the immobilizer pre-release password.
limits: No licence: all rights reserved.

sources.name: emdzej/ediabasx-docs-sgbd (cited by the project's own candidate family.bmw-mini.cbs-reset)
sources.kind: documentation of BMW diagnostic description files
sources.licence: none (the GitHub API reports no licence for the repository)
sources.accessed: 2026-10-19 (the job index and the CBS_RESET job of the d72n47a0 page; 300,000 of 618,000 characters)
sources.read: Job index and the CBS_RESET job: UDS 2E; arguments CBS_KENNUNG (item: Oel, Br_v, Br_h, NOx_a, Brfl, Sic, Sic_v, TUV, AU, Ueb, Efk), availability percentage, number of services, target month and year, remaining distance with unit, forecast distance and time intervals; CBS_RESET_DATEN_LESEN reads DID 0x4050; STEUERN_CBS_DATEN_SICHERN is routine F0ED (31 01), its status 31 03 F0ED; STATUS_CBSMOTOROELHIST 22 404F; STATUS_CODIERUNG_OEL 22 3701. The identifier that CBS_RESET writes is not shown.
sources.use: Read for research only; nothing is used. The page derives from BMW's proprietary description file and carries no licence.
limits: No licence. The content derives from BMW's proprietary description files.

sources.name: Hella / Pagid, BMW CBS brake-pad reset (techtips.ie PDF) and related workshop pages
sources.read: Search summary only: CBS brake-pad parameters can be reset with a diagnostic unit or in the cluster; a commercial tool resets CBS oil service. (BMW's own bulletins were read in full: see bmw-si-b620613.)
sources.use: Context only: the function exists in closed tools.
limits: No routine id, no payload.

sources.name: Workshop blogs on the ASSYST reset (kfz-dietrich.com, blog.usro.net)
sources.read: The summary: the reset is a XENTRY service function or a cluster key sequence; the blogs disagree on the menu path; a plain UDS 0x14 clear affects fault memory only.
sources.use: Not used. No official or open routine was found.
limits: Low-quality and contradictory.

sources.name: eeNews Europe, 'Diagnostic tester detects mileage manipulation' (26 January 2021)
sources.read: The article: a Bosch tester function lists the mileage stored in various control units (the seat memory and the electronic parking assistant are named) and compares it with the speedometer reading.
sources.use: Shows that several modules store mileage and that comparison is done by commercial tools. No protocol; no module list beyond the two named.
limits: A mismatch is presented by the article as a sign of possible manipulation; this app reports it as an observation with the other explanations.

sources.name: iamcarhacker.com, OBD2 mileage check guides (including a Skoda Octavia case)
sources.read: The summary: engine, ABS and body modules are named as holders of mileage; some cars store mileage only in the cluster; in one case a transmission module read about three times the dashboard value and was judged a corrupted counter rather than real mileage.
sources.use: Supports the rule that a difference is an observation, never a verdict.
limits: Single-author blog; second-hand.

sources.name: General UDS references (Wikipedia 'Unified Diagnostic Services', python-uds / kiso-testing documentation)
sources.read: Service ids (0x22 read, 0x2E write by identifier, 0x19 read DTC information) and the usual session / security-access sequence. Nothing names an oil-service or odometer identifier; those are manufacturer-defined (the ISO 14229-1 identifier annex is paid and was not read).
sources.use: Context for the protocol vocabulary only.
limits: No evidence that DTC snapshots carry the odometer.

sources.name: Resources/Raw/service_procedures.json (this repository)
sources.read: All 165 procedures (164 when first read, 165 after the Mazda CX-5 SKYACTIV-D guide of 2026-10-19): manual, SourceDocumented, dashboard verification, from owner's manuals and manufacturer documents; none VehicleVerified.
sources.use: The guided-reset side of service-operation-coverage.json.
limits: Its own coverage notes: a missing vehicle means no sufficiently specific source has been pinned yet, not that no procedure exists.

sources.name: Resources/Raw/oem_operations.json (this repository)
sources.read: operations is empty; 12 family and 73 vehicle research candidates, all non-executable, with the promotion checklist.
sources.use: The gate this research keeps: no write operation without exact per-vehicle evidence.
limits: Generated 2026-09-20.

sources.name: SERVICE_RESET_RESEARCH.md (this repository, 2026-09)
sources.read: The project's comparison of 14 scanner apps and its verification audit of 2026-09-28: oil/service reset is not part of SAE J1979; apps send only the verified command of the identified car; no open database of reset commands exists; the generic 22 -> 2E write for GM 4DC0, Ford 054B and Mazda 0519 and the inferred GMLAN $3B write-back were disabled. The notes also say the GM reset was done on a Volt 2013.
sources.use: Agrees with this research, which reached the same conclusions from other sources. Its claim of a working Volt reset has no capture or evidence file, so it is not used as evidence.
limits: Dated 2026-09; the app comparison is from vendor pages, not from tests.

sources.name: DIAGNOSTIC_MODULES_MILEAGE_SERVICE_AUDIT.md (this repository)
sources.read: Four capture files (Volt 2013, BMW 320i 2018, Ford Escape 2012, Toyota Camry) recorded by the app: PID A6 returned NO DATA in all four; BMW 19 04 got NO DATA; vehicle identity is a label, not an established fact.
sources.evidence: observation only (the audit itself says: not verification)
sources.use: The only vehicle observations in the repository. Cited where they bear on a source.
limits: Observations of unreviewed captures; identity not established.

sources.name: OBD360_OVERNIGHT_REPORT_2026-10-18.md (this repository)
sources.read: States that no automatic oil reset is enabled for any car (ReviewedGmOilLifeResets empty since the 2026-09-28 safety audit) and documents the first-generation Volt read path (22 119F, then 4DC0).
sources.use: Baseline of the Service page before this work.

sources.name: OBDb recorded test replies (tests/test_cases/<model year>/commands/*.yaml and command_support.yaml in every vehicle repository)
sources.licenceChecked: 2026-10-19 through the GitHub API (all 880 vehicle repositories)
sources.read: All 860 downloaded repositories parsed by research/tools/evidence-obdb.js: per signal and model year, whether the command applies (filter), is still debug (dbg, dbgfilter), is listed as supported (command_support.yaml) and has recorded replies with the values OBDb expects them to decode to.
sources.evidence: E4 (a reply recorded for that model year; recorded by contributors, not by OBD360)
sources.use: Derived tables only: research/obdb-evidence-*.json and .md, research/oil-life-capability-matrix.*, and the compact Resources/Raw/obdb_year_evidence.json the app reads. The raw repositories are not in this repository.
limits: The model year is the folder name; OBDb does not say how it was determined.
Replies of different commands may come from different cars.
A missing reply does not make a definition wrong.

sources.name: GM Customer Satisfaction Program 12312A, 'Oil Life Monitor Update', August 2013 (NHTSA files MC-10114191-9999 and MC-10246678-9999, the same text)
sources.accessed: 2026-10-19 (downloaded, converted with pdftotext, read in full)
sources.read: 2010-2011 Buick LaCrosse, 2011-2012 Buick Regal, 2010-2012 Chevrolet Equinox and GMC Terrain with the 2.4L engine (RPO LAF, LEA, LUK): reprogram the engine control module, then 'use a scan tool to reset the Engine Oil Life Remaining back to the original percentage recorded before'.
sources.use: The one documented case of a maker's tool setting a chosen oil-life percentage. Names the executing module (engine control module). No request is published.
limits: The scan tool is not named; a restored percentage is not proof that other engines accept a chosen value.

sources.name: GM Service Bulletin 18-NA-125 (May 2024), PIP5282A (September 2016) and PIP6076 (June 2025)
sources.read: The oil life monitor calculates the percentage from engine revolutions, mileage since the reset (capped at 7,500 miles from model year 2013, Volt excepted) and time (one year; two for the Volt); it starts after the first 50 miles and restarts at each reset. PIP6076: the Corvette transmission fluid life has its own reset, and after it the percentage may drop quickly (under investigation).
sources.use: What a post-reset read-back should show and why the value then falls; that transmission oil life is a separate reset item.

sources.name: BMW SI B62 06 13, Condition Based Service due date is reset to 01/2000 (February 2014: MC-10147976-9999; May 2014: MC-10148333-9999)
sources.read: F01, F02, F04, F06, F07, F10, F12, F13, F25 and F30 cars: the CBS due dates for 'Oil Services' and 'Check Vehicle' fall back to 01/2000 because of a software error in the instrument cluster; the correction is the cluster's test function #25 'Software reset' (hold the left soft key for more than 10 seconds), then setting the date, then checking the CBS data on the CID; if still wrong, the ISTA/D test plan for resetting and adjusting the CBS data.
sources.evidence: E3 (where CBS lives and that ISTA has a test plan), E0 (request)
sources.use: Shows that the CBS data of these cars is held in the instrument cluster and that test function #25 is a repair, not a service reset.

sources.name: Kia TSB ELE209 (Rev 3, 16 August 2022), 'Service reminder setting reset procedure' (MC-10217892-0001; first issue MC-10180656-0001)
sources.read: 2019MY and later Kia: with the dealer tool KDS, 'Cluster Module', 'S/W Management', 'Service Reminder Setting': change the service type from workshop to customer and enter the mileage and time.
sources.use: The service reminder of these cars is set in the instrument cluster by a dealer tool function.
limits: Dealer tool only (KDS with a VCI-II).

sources.name: Kia TSB ENG241 (September 2022), 'Oil life management system (OLMS) and maintenance reminder feature' (MC-10220347-0001)
sources.read: 2023MY and later with OLMS: the oil life is set to 100% at the factory; the owner resets it from the head unit ('Vehicle Settings', 'Cluster', 'Oil Change Reminder', 'Reset') after an oil change, and the remaining oil life is shown there.
sources.use: An owner-level oil-life reset that needs no tool; consistent with the shipped Kia guides.

sources.name: Stellantis STAR case S2309000009, 'GG/GC Oil Change Monitor Reset' (October 2023; NHTSA file MC-10247449-9999)
sources.read: After an oil change, with the scan tool: in the instrument panel cluster ('IPC'), 'Miscellaneous Functions', run the 'Reset Service Information' routine; and in the PCM, 'Miscellaneous Functions', run the 'Reset oil change indicator' procedure.
sources.use: Names the two modules and the two routines the dealer tool runs for the vehicles of the case.
limits: The vehicles of the case are named only by the codes GG and GC.

sources.name: Mazda CX-5 owner's manual, 'Vehicle Engine Control Unit Reset Procedure (SKYACTIV-D 2.2)' (2018 and 2017 editions)
sources.accessed: 2026-10-19 (the 2018 page read in full; the 2017 edition is a separate page of the same title, not fetched)
sources.read: 'Engine oil data resetting' initializes the oil value recorded by the computer after an oil change; otherwise the wrench indicator may stay on or come on early. Driver method: ignition off, then on while the instrument-panel illumination knob is pressed, hold about 5 seconds until the master warning light flashes, wait for it to flash for several seconds. The manual also recommends having a repairer do it.
sources.use: The new shipped guide mazda.cx5.2017-2018.skyactiv-d-oil-data-reset.
limits: The 2017 edition was not opened; the guide is limited to the years of the manuals found (2017-2018) and to diesel.

sources.name: Ford TSB 22-2484 and SSM 49728 (2021 F-150 5.0L, PCM update and oil change reminder reset)
sources.accessed: 2026-10-19 (search summaries only; the PDFs were not opened)
sources.read: The summaries say that after the PCM is reprogrammed and the oil changed the technician resets the engine oil change reminder 'referring to the vehicle Owner's Manual'.
sources.use: Context: Ford's own bulletins treat the reminder reset as an owner's-manual step.
limits: Second-hand; confirm in the PDFs.

sources.name: Mercedes-Benz Sprinter maintenance booklets 2010-2014 (mbvans.com)
sources.read: The summaries say the authorized dealer resets the ASSYST service interval display after every maintenance service and that resetting it without the service may cause engine damage.
sources.use: Who resets ASSYST on the Sprinter.
limits: Second-hand; confirm in the booklets.

sources.name: Lexus bulletin T-SB-0022-23 (May 2023; NHTSA MC-10238134-9999)
sources.read: The summary says the Maintenance Required reminder is cleared from the multi-information display's vehicle settings menu and that Techstream appears in such bulletins for other jobs.
sources.use: Where the Toyota/Lexus reminder is cleared.
limits: Second-hand; confirm in the PDF.

sources.name: Honda and Acura bulletins 23-073 (MC-10242219-0001) and 14-049 (MC-10110849-9999)
sources.read: The summaries name the older HDS path 'Body Electrical, Adjustment, Maintenance Minder, Reset, maintenance sub-item' and, for newer cars, i-HDS or the multi-information display depending on the item.
sources.use: Where the Honda Maintenance Minder is reset.
limits: Second-hand; confirm in the PDFs.

sources.name: FORScan forum threads on oil resets (t=19160, t=21428; t=18282 and t=17187 returned HTTP 403)
sources.accessed: 2026-10-19 (the two readable threads read in full)
sources.read: No hex requests, identifiers or logs are posted. A poster says that on a Mazda 5 diesel FORScan's service procedure resets the learned oil dilution value and shows the dilution in grams.
sources.use: The meaning of 'Reset Engine Oil Deterioration Learned Value' on Mazda diesels (oil dilution, not a percentage of oil life).
limits: Single forum posters.

sources.name: Car Scanner ELM OBD2, coding and service functions page
sources.read: Names a 'Reset service reminder' function for GM with CAN bus (Opel, Chevrolet, Vauxhall, Holden) and CVT oil degradation resets for some Mitsubishi and Nissan models; shows no service id, identifier or byte.
sources.use: Existence of a GM service-reminder function in a consumer app; nothing more.
limits: No protocol detail on the page.
